record.paper_title: Magic matrices with their powers, numerical ranges and some open problems
record.original_question: Let a magic matrix of order n mean an n by n square matrix whose entries are the natural numbers 1, 2, ..., n^2 with no repeated entry, and whose row sums, column sums, main diagonal sum, and antidiagonal sum are all equal. Is it true in general that magic matrices of odd order have full rank, whereas magic matrices of even order have rank strictly smaller than their order?

evidence.quote: square matrices (of order n) satisfying the following conditions: (m1) the entries aij of A belong to the set {1, 2, . . . , n2 }, (m2) if (i, j) 6= (k, l) then aij 6= akl , (m3) the sums in each row, each column, main diagonal and antidiagonal are equal.
Open problem 2. Magic matrices of odd order seem to be of full rank, while magic matrices of even order seem to have rank strictly smaller than their order. Is that true in general?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a magic matrix of order $n$ to be an $n\times n$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ with real entries such that:
(i) every entry $a_{ij}$ belongs to $\{1,2,\ldots,n^{2}\}$;
(ii) all entries are distinct, i.e. $a_{ij}\neq a_{kl}$ whenever $(i,j)\neq(k,l)$;
(iii) the sum of the entries in each row, in each column, on the main diagonal, and on the antidiagonal are all equal (necessarily to $n(n^{2}+1)/2$).

Decide whether the following statement holds:

For every magic matrix $A$ of order $n$, if $n$ is odd then $\operatorname{rank}(A)=n$, and if $n$ is even then $\operatorname{rank}(A)<n$.

Either prove the statement, or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: Empirical observations and discussions (e.g., Cleve Moler's notes on magic squares in MATLAB) report that odd-order magic squares appear to have full rank, doubly-even ones tend to have rank 3, and singly-even ones have intermediate rank, but a complete proof for arbitrary magic matrices satisfying the stated definition does not appear to be established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Magic Squares, Part 3, Linear Algebra - Cleve's Corner
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of ranks of magic squares: odd order full rank, doubly even rank 3, singly even rank n/2+2, based on MATLAB's magic() construction.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical/structural observations support the conjecture for standard constructions, but a general proof for all magic matrices is not given.
